c0002: ASSUMPTIONS — the RATES and DRIVERS of the model are typed here
c0003: Change the GREEN cells: the rest of the workbook recalculates on its own. Expense items are typed on their own tab (also in green) and are not repeated here. Amounts are in your currency.
c0016: SALES MIX AND COST OF GOODS SOLD
c0018: Share of FOOD in total sales. It is an INPUT: change it here and the P&L, the cash flow and the sales tax collected recalculate on their own
c0020: Calculated as the remainder: food + beverage = 100%
c0021: Cost of goods sold on FOOD sales
c0023: Cost of goods sold on BEVERAGE sales
c0025: Disposables and packaging as % of sales
c0035: FICA (Social Security 6.2% + Medicare 1.45%) + federal and state unemployment taxes (FUTA / SUTA) + workers' comp. About 10% in total: adjust it to your state and your insurance carrier
c0037: Annual gross pay = monthly gross pay × this number. Keep 12 in the US: it counts the monthly salaries the model pays in a year, not how often you run payroll (weekly or biweekly payroll pays the same annual amount)
c0039: US federal minimum wage: 7.25 per hour × 2,080 hours = 15,080 per year for a full-time job. Your state or city may set a higher floor: enter it in the state / local minimum wage cell below. Check the current rates at dol.gov
c0049: Miscellaneous and contingency as % of sales
c0066: Example: 21% federal rate for a C corporation plus state tax, rounded to 25%. If you operate as a sole proprietorship, LLC taxed as a pass-through or S corporation, the business itself pays 0% here and you pay tax on the profit personally: set this to 0 and budget for your personal tax separately. The model applies this rate to the first two years with positive taxable income
c0068: From the third year with positive taxable income. Same example rate (21% federal C corporation + state). Confirm the rate that applies to you with your accountant and change it here
c0070: Example rate: state + local sales tax combined. It varies widely by state and city: look up yours. UK: 20% VAT on hot food and dine-in
c0074: In the US, the sales tax you pay on purchases is a cost, not a credit: leave this at 0%. UK: 20% if you are VAT-registered
c0076: Net operating losses from earlier years still to be offset at the start. Federal rules let you offset up to 80% of taxable income in a year; the model offsets 100% as a simplification
c0078: Useful life of build-out and fixtures (years)
c0080: Useful life of machinery, furniture and equipment (years)
c0084: SET TO ZERO: all three columns are in year-1 prices (real terms). Raise it if you want to project in nominal terms
c0088: Month-1 activity as a % of steady-state activity
c0092: Months of rent BEFORE opening (build-out and permits)
c0094: Contingency on the BUILD-OUT lines of the space block (%)
c0096: RECEIPTS, PAYMENTS AND SALES TAX BREAKDOWN
c0101: Month of extra pay period 1 (only if pay periods > 12)
c0103: Month of extra pay period 2 (only if pay periods > 12)
c0111: Below 1.0 the business does not generate enough to repay the loan. Lenders often write a minimum DSCR into the loan covenants: ask yours. Kit default: 1.15×
c0113: What lenders commonly look for before approving a loan comfortably. Kit default: 1.25× (editable estimate)
c0115: How far planned sales must sit above cash break-even (fixed costs and the loan payment). The drop you can absorb is somewhat smaller: with a 15% cushion, about 13% of plan
c0120: Enter a number greater than or equal to 0.
c0126: Whole years of interest-only period, from 0 to 15. If it equals or exceeds the loan term, the sheet ignores it.
c0128: Month of the year, from 1 to 12.
c0129: Loan term in whole years: the amortization schedule in this workbook runs up to 15 years.
c0130: Useful life in WHOLE YEARS (1 to 50). Depreciation here is straight-line book depreciation; tax rules such as MACRS or Section 179 are separate.
c0131: Enter a WHOLE number of 1 or more: this cell is a count and several formulas divide by it.
c0132: Monthly pay periods per year, from 12 to 16. Keep 12 in the US: it is not your payroll frequency. Extra pay periods apply only if you enter more than 12.
c0186: TOTAL STARTUP COSTS (sum of the blocks)
c0188: What you buy: build-out, equipment, launch and formation costs. The cash cushion is not an investment: it is working capital
c0191: This is the figure the Financing tab has to cover
c0192: DEPRECIATION BASES (not added to startup costs)
c0197: Enter "Yes" or "No": the recoverable input tax on startup costs comes from this column.
c0205: Sales tax rate on the line (%)
c0209: Growth for years 2 and 3 is set in "0. Assumptions"
c0211: Held constant at year-1 prices: a price increase is a separate decision
c0222: Applied to the sales of THAT CHANNEL. With 0% delivery in Assumptions, this line is zero
c0224: Card processing fees are not subject to sales tax: no tax is recovered or deducted for them
c0232: Comes from the Staffing tab: it is the SAME number, not a separate estimate. Years 2 and 3 add the new hires declared on that tab, not a percentage of volume
c0234: Enter the monthly bills excl. sales tax. The workbook applies a single tax treatment to this whole line, the one in the column next to it; if one utility is taxed differently in your area, give it its own line
c0236: Insurance premiums are not subject to sales tax: there is no recoverable tax on them
c0256: Comes from the depreciation bases on the Startup Costs tab: real fixed assets only. It does NOT rise with inflation: it is a charge on the HISTORICAL cost of the assets
c0258: Only INTEREST is an expense. Principal repaid appears on the cash flow tab
c0260: Recoverable input tax on variable costs
c0261: Each line at ITS OWN rate, read from the column next to it. It is what the cash flow tab overpays to suppliers and later deducts (zero wherever no tax is recoverable)
c0262: Recoverable input tax on fixed costs
c0265: Federal rules let a year's losses offset the profits of later years (the federal limit is 80% of taxable income; this model offsets 100% as a simplification)
c0269: The "years 1-2" rate applies to the first two years with positive taxable income, not to the first two calendar years of the business. The model approximates this by counting the first two profitable years
c0289: Compares each year's sales with that same year's threshold, which the Break-Even tab calculates with that year's fixed costs
c0290: All figures are EXCL. SALES TAX. Years 2 and 3 are in year-1 prices unless you raise cost inflation in the "0. Assumptions" tab. The "Sales tax rate on the line (%)" column shows, on SALES lines, the rate collected on each one and, on COST lines, the rate paid on that item. The cash flow tab reads it: insurance and card fees carry no sales tax, and wages, depreciation and interest carry none either.
c0297: The SAME fixed costs as the P&L. Each year has its own, which is why the threshold cannot be a single one for all three years
c0300: Comes from the P&L total variable costs, not from a separate estimate. It includes miscellaneous and contingency, which is a percentage of sales
c0302: Average check minus unit variable cost
c0303: The same calendar as the P&L and the scenarios
c0305: Principal is NOT a P&L expense, but it leaves the cash account. Without it, the published break-even threshold would sit below the real one
c0310: CASH BREAK-EVEN (loan payments in, depreciation out)
c0311: Cash fixed costs + principal repaid for the year
c0312: The P&L fixed costs without depreciation (which is not paid in cash) and WITH principal repaid (which is). This is the threshold that decides whether cash holds up
c0319: How far planned sales sit above cash break-even. The drop you can absorb before you cannot pay the fixed costs and the loan payment is somewhat smaller: with a 25% cushion, 20%. The required minimum is set in the "0. Assumptions" tab
c0334: Fixed costs do not change with the scenario: that is why they are fixed
c0335: At the "years 1-2" effective income tax rate, offsetting prior net operating losses
c0338: The SAME staffing in all three scenarios. If labor cost blows up in the pessimistic case, adjust it in the Staffing tab, not here
c0341: Year-1 closing cash balance (estimate, same method in all three scenarios)
c0342: ESTIMATED balance: working capital plus the year's result, adding back depreciation (which is not paid) and subtracting loan principal. It does not include the timing gap between receipts and payments or the sales tax settlement, so the three columns can be compared with each other. In red, the scenario runs out of cash
c0343: Actual month-12 balance from the 12-Month Cash Flow tab (Base case only)
c0344: The ACTUAL base-case balance, with its timing of receipts and payments and its sales tax settlement. It exists only for the Base scenario, the only one with its own monthly cash flow: that is why it is not in the row above, where it would be compared against two estimates
c0351: Gross pay per month (total for the position)
c0352: Employer payroll taxes (total for the position)
c0353: Cost per month (total for the position)
c0356: Hours per year for the position
c0374: FULL ANNUAL cost (gross pay + employer payroll taxes, over all pay periods) of whoever you hire that year. The P&L adds it to the previous year's cost: staffing grows by people, not by a percentage
c0380: 40 hours a week is the FLSA overtime threshold for non-exempt employees; some states add daily overtime rules. Change it if your own full-time week is different
c0381: Weeks worked per year per person
c0382: 46 weeks: 52 minus about six weeks for vacation, holidays and average absences. There is no federal vacation requirement in the US: adjust it to your own policy
c0383: Service hours per day to cover
c0385: People needed at the same time in each shift
c0387: Production hours per day BEFORE opening
c0391: Service hours to cover per year
c0394: Below 100% the staff cannot cover the hours the plan declares: either hire more or cut the hours
c0396: The pay floor is the HIGHER of the federal minimum wage and your state / local minimum wage, both in the "0. Assumptions" tab; part-time positions get it in proportion. There is no single national table above the federal floor: the state / local cell is delivered empty so you can enter the rate for your state and city.
c0398: Enter a number greater than or equal to 0; this cell accepts decimals (1.7 people is an average presence, not a person and a half).
c0402: This financial plan is a MODEL: you type only in the GREEN cells and everything else recalculates on its own.
c0404: 2. Startup cost items, fixed costs and staffing are typed in their own tab, also in green. No number is typed twice.
c0407: 5. If you change the staffing, the P&L reads it on its own: labor cost comes from the "Staffing" tab, not from a separate estimate.
c0412: Thresholds live in the "Threshold" column of the KEY RATIOS block of the P&L: change them there and the traffic light changes with them.
c0416: Total startup costs (sum of the blocks)
c0482: The P&L tells you whether the business makes money; this tab tells you whether you have cash left to get to the end of the month. It is the first one a lender looks at.
c0499: Rises in a straight line from the month-1 percentage to 100% over the number of months you set in Assumptions. With month 1 at 100%, the ramp disappears
c0501: Seasonality × ramp-up, normalized to 100%: the YEAR brings in what the P&L says, but split the way a business that has just opened would split it
c0504: The month's sales plus the sales tax collected, adjusted by the average collection days from the Assumptions tab
c0506: Purchases and variable costs (incl. sales tax)
c0508: The fixed costs that leave cash, each with its own tax rate: insurance carries none
c0510: Twelve monthly installments plus extra pay periods in the months you set in Assumptions (only if pay periods > 12). The total for the year is the same as the P&L's
c0516: Each item at its own rate, read from the tax column of the P&L: insurance and card processing fees carry none
c0518: Sales tax paid on STARTUP COSTS enters here: it is offset against the tax collected in later quarters until used up. With 0% recoverable input tax (the US default) this line stays at zero
c0520: Sales tax collected minus recoverable input tax for the quarter, minus what was carried forward. If negative, nothing is paid: it is offset in the next quarter. With 0% recoverable input tax (the US default) it equals the sales tax collected in the quarter
c0522: Cash only leaves when the quarter's result is positive. Months without a settlement are left blank, not zero. The cell turns RED when the payment takes more cash than is left that month. The model settles quarterly, in the month after each plan quarter (Months 4, 7 and 10: April, July and October with Month 1 in January; the fourth quarter is remitted in Month 13, January of the next year): if your state requires monthly filing, expect smaller payments every month instead
c0526: If negative, raise working capital or the loan: you run out of cash
c0528: It answers the question that decides a bank deal: in which month the cash runs out
c0530: Free cash flow before debt, year 1
c0531: Net income plus depreciation (which is not paid) plus that year's interest: principal is not subtracted because this flow is BEFORE debt. The SAME basis as years 2 and 3, so the payback compares like with like
c0532: Free cash flow before debt, year 2
c0533: Net income plus depreciation (which is not paid) plus that year's interest: principal is not subtracted because this flow is BEFORE debt. Without a monthly table, it is an estimate
c0534: Free cash flow before debt, year 3
c0535: For reference: ACTUAL year-1 cash flow (monthly table, before debt)
c0536: The sum of the twelve monthly net cash flows above, adding back the interest and principal paid that year. It is NOT the one the payback uses: it includes sales tax not yet settled and supplier credit, two things that have to be paid back and that years 2 and 3 do not have
c0537: Investment to recover (net of recoverable input tax)
c0538: CAPEX plus working capital: the total cash needed MINUS the recoverable input tax on startup costs, which is not lost (it is recovered through the quarterly return, and this tab offsets it quarter by quarter; it is zero in the US default). Working capital is recovered when you close, but until then it is tied up
c0540: Payback on CAPEX, excluding working capital (years)
c0541: The same calculation on what you BUY (build-out, equipment, launch and formation costs), without working capital: that money is not spent, it is tied up and comes back when the business closes. For reference only: the payback that matters is the one above
c0542: Fourth-quarter sales tax is settled in Month 13 (January of the following year when Month 1 is January), so it does not appear in this table. The model pays year-1 income tax in July of year 2 (a simplification: estimated tax payments are usually quarterly). The loan payment is spread in twelve equal parts following the ANNUAL schedule in the Financing tab, and payroll in twelve monthly installments (plus extra pay periods in their month, only if pay periods > 12).
c0545: What you need, where it comes from and what it costs to repay. It is the sheet your lender asks for along with the P&L.
c0548: Loan requested — bank or SBA 7(a) (amortized below)
c0550: A source of funds only: NOT amortized, so it is not in the schedule, the P&L interest or the DSCR. Enter your bank or SBA 7(a) loan in row 7 ("Loan requested" in "0. Assumptions"); use this row only for a second loan
c0552: SBA Microloans go up to $50,000 through nonprofit intermediaries. Like row 8, a source of funds only: not in the schedule or the DSCR. If it is your only loan, enter it in row 7 instead
c0554: Equity: it dilutes your ownership and is not repaid
c0556: Usually paid AFTER you document the spending
c0559: Startup costs plus any recoverable tax you have to advance (zero by default in the US)
c0561: In red (negative), the plan is NOT funded. Far above zero is not free either: you pay interest on money you do not use
c0563: Amber above the margin you set: it is debt you pay for without needing it
c0565: A small cushion over the need is healthy; 20% extra is interest thrown away
c0566: Loan that would match sources to needs
c0567: Copy it into "Loan requested" in the "0. Assumptions" tab and the difference goes to zero. Rows 8-11 lower this figure, but only the row-7 loan is amortized and counted in the DSCR
c0572: An interest-only period equal to or longer than the term does not exist: the sheet cancels it at the source
c0574: Standard amortizing loan with a level annual payment. At a 0% rate it is the principal divided by the repayment years: without that branch the schedule would shut down entirely
c0582: Cash flow available for debt service (after tax; from year 4 on, year 3 held flat)
c0585: Rounding margin. Above it, the schedule does not close and there is principal left unpaid
c0587: Must be zero: the principal repaid in the schedule has to equal the amount borrowed. If it is positive, the term falls short
c0596: An INTEREST-ONLY year, if there is one: with only interest in the denominator the ratio shoots up and does not measure the business
c0599: Minimum DSCR across the whole schedule
c0600: The worst year of the life of the loan, not the best of the three the P&L projects. It is the number that decides a loan. Mind the scope: years 1 to 3 come from the P&L, and from year 4 on the schedule HOLDS year 3's cash flow, so the minimum over those years is a sustained projection, not a calculated year. The cash flow is after tax
c0601: DSCR is calculated BEFORE debt and AFTER tax: income tax is subtracted from pre-tax income, depreciation and interest are added back, and the result is divided by what has to be paid that year. Below the minimum in the "0. Assumptions" tab, the business does not generate enough to repay the loan. In the schedule, the available cash flow from year 4 on is held at year 3's: the P&L projects only three years, and no growth is invented here that has not been calculated.
c0852: The GREEN cells are the editable ones: change those and the rest of the workbook recalculates on its own.
c0853: OK column: choose ✓ (done), ☐ (pending) or N/A (not applicable). N/A items do not count toward the total.
c0854: Each tab's counter counts only the ✓; N/A items come out of the total.
